text:
Celine: Dropped a 'slate-contrast-mapping' theme in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/slate-contrast-mapping. Purpose: clearer micro-UI contrast w/o brightening the whole shell. Focus: legends, mini-sparklines, badges, inline code, and chart stacking. Quick eyes please.
Harper: First glance: mini legend swatches at 12px are ambiguous when there are 5+ series. Two options: enlarge swatch to 14px or enable hover-to-highlight. Hover seems less layout-breaking.
Noah: Hover-to-highlight + keyboard-list fallback (accessible legend view) 👍. Also stacked bars: current hue ramp has too-small lightness deltas. Propose a Lab L* based ramp with bigger L differences.
Vik: For tiny badge counters (8px) we should add a subtle halo/backdrop rather than increasing size to avoid layout shifts. Example CSS: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.18) inset;` keeps the visual weight low.
June: Inline code in comments is low-contrast on some monitors. Suggest left accent bar plus semi-bold text rather than filled chips. CSS: `.inline-code{border-left:2px solid var(--accent);padding-left:6px;background:transparent;font-weight:600}`
Celine: Noted on badges and inline code. I'll prototype halo for badges and left-bar inline-code. For charts: thinking of a "contrast mapping" mode that maps series to both color and a subtle pattern (dotted/diagonal) for stacked bars as an enterprise opt-in.
Harper: Pattern overlay is powerful but could get noisy in small thumbnails. Maybe pattern only in hover/legend-expansion or when user enables high-contrast mode.
Noah: Agreed. Also for sparklines at 6-9px, thin strokes vanish on 1x. Propose an outer stroke using panel-contrast color (opacity ~0.9) for thumbnails only. And a slightly thicker trailing cap to highlight current value.
Vik: Microcopy: tooltips use both "units" and "tokens" across views. Let's standardize to "tokens" everywhere and update i18n keys.
June: Accessibility: add `aria-label` to chart toggles e.g. `aria-label="Chart: hourly token usage"` and `aria-pressed` so screen readers get context. Also focus rings for table rows need stronger contrast: `outline:3px solid rgba(80,160,255,0.92); outline-offset:4px`.
Celine: Good call. Also which accent direction do folks prefer: slightly mauve-leaning (cool) or teal-leaning (neutral)? I'm leaning mauve because it separates from warm error red.
Harper: Mauve is nice but ensure strings in code blocks don't clash. For syntax highlighting: keys = #C7B3FF (mauve), strings = #97D89A (soft green), numbers = #7FC9FF. That keeps errors (red) distinct.
Noah: Love the syntax swap. One more thought: add a per-user "Chart contrast" slider in Settings (0-100) that adjusts accent lightness and pattern opacity. Advanced users can fine-tune.
Vik: Slider is neat, but we should also ship a set of presets (Default / High contrast / Reduced color) for non-power users. Remember preference per-user.
June: Also ensure the slider has accessible labels and keyboard support. Aria-describedby should explain what changes on change.
Celine: I'll prototype presets + a slider for advanced settings. If folks can skim the figma and leave short comments (or :thumbsup:) I'll cut a small token PR today.
Theme-Bot: Design review created: DR-4722 - "Slate contrast mapping: legends, sparklines, badges, and a11y patterns" assigned to @Celine. Comments due in 72h.
Harper: Leaving a few Figma notes on legend hover and the pattern samples.
Noah: I'll run Axe contrast pass after tokens land and post results here.
Celine: Thanks all — will post updated tokens + changelog later today.
